title: Aleksei Navalny and the Future of Russia

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, a standoff between President Vladimir Putin and his loudest critic turned into a showdown in the streets of Russia.
sentences.zh: 周末期间，弗拉基米尔·普京总统与其最直言不讳的批评者之间的对峙，演变成了俄罗斯街头的公开较量。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Anton Choyanovsky with the improbable story of Alexei Navalny.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事安东·特罗亚诺夫斯基将讲述阿列克谢·纳瓦利内那不可思议的故事。

sentences.en: It's Monday, January 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月25日，星期一。

sentences.en: Anton, tell me about Alexei Navalny.
sentences.zh: 安东，跟我讲讲阿列克谢·纳瓦利内吧。

sentences.en: So he's a real estate lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他是一名房地产律师。

sentences.en: He's 44 years old.
sentences.zh: 今年44岁。

sentences.en: He got his start around 2007 as a shareholder rights activiSt.
sentences.zh: 他大约在2007年开始以股东权利活动家的身份崭露头角。

sentences.en: He would buy small numbers of shares in various Russian state-owned companies and then sue them for information that he would then put on a blog
sentences.zh: 他会购买俄罗斯各家国有企业少量的股份，然后起诉它们以获取信息，并将这些信息发布在博客上，

sentences.en: that quickly became widely read among people in the finance industry in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 这些博客很快在莫斯科金融界广为流传。

sentences.en: So more and more, he made a name for himself as an anti-corruption activist, kind of investigating the hidden wealth of the Russian elite,
sentences.zh: 因此，他作为一名反腐败活动家逐渐声名鹊起，开始调查俄罗斯精英阶层隐藏的财富，

sentences.en: the questionable financial transactions made by Russian officials and people close to them.
sentences.zh: 以及俄罗斯官员及其亲信进行的各种可疑金融交易。

sentences.en: And he increasingly started dabbling in politics.
sentences.zh: 他开始越来越多地涉足政治。

sentences.en: And his breakout moment as a politician came in 2011.
sentences.zh: 他作为政治人物的突破性时刻出现在2011年。

sentences.en: That was back when Putin announces that he's going to run for president again, which was a big shock to a lot of people in Russia
sentences.zh: 当时普京宣布将再次竞选总统，这对俄罗斯许多人来说是一个巨大的冲击，

sentences.en: who had hoped that the country would see a more liberal turn.
sentences.zh: 因为他们曾希望国家能走向更自由的道路。

sentences.en: And you have this big explosion of protests that Navalny ends up leading.
sentences.zh: 随后爆发了大规模的抗议活动，而纳瓦利内最终成为了领导者。

sentences.en: He becomes someone who can get thousands of people out into the streets, you know, with his Twitter posts, with his blog posts.
sentences.zh: 他成了那种能通过推特和博客文章号召成千上万民众走上街头的人。

sentences.en: He gets thrown in jail for a few weeks, but that doesn't stop the protests from continuing.
sentences.zh: 他被关进监狱几周，但这并没有阻止抗议活动的继续。

sentences.en: So he really builds a platform that way as a politician.
sentences.zh: 所以，他确实以这种方式建立了自己的政治平台。

sentences.en: He is not universally appreciated, even by Putin's critics.
sentences.zh: 他并非受到普遍认可，即使在普京的批评者中也是如此。

sentences.en: A lot of liberals in Moscow had a problem with his nationalist views.
sentences.zh: 莫斯科的许多自由派人士对他的民族主义观点颇有微词。

sentences.en: He was also known for some pretty xenophobic things he would say about immigrants from Central Asia or people from the North Caucasus.
sentences.zh: 他还因针对中亚移民或北高加索地区人士发表过一些相当排外的言论而闻名。

sentences.en: So he's quite a controversial figure.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个极具争议的人物。

sentences.en: But he's really someone who, unlike most Putin opponents, unlike most Russian liberals, he's really someone who can speak to a broad cross-section of people.
sentences.zh: 但他确实与大多数普京的反对者、大多数俄罗斯自由派不同，他是一个真正能与各阶层民众对话的人。

sentences.en: It sounds like he's a very successful agitator.
sentences.zh: 听起来他是一位非常成功的煽动者。

sentences.en: Absolutely, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是，绝对是。

sentences.en: And we saw that in 2013, he runs for mayor of Moscow.
sentences.zh: 我们在2013年看到了这一点，他竞选莫斯科市长。

sentences.en: And even though, you know, he's largely barred from the airwaves, he's running against Putin's former chief of staff, he still gets 27% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 尽管他基本上被禁止在媒体上发声，而且对手是普京的前办公厅主任，但他依然获得了27%的选票。

sentences.en: And that's a lot in Russia for an opposition figure.
sentences.zh: 在俄罗斯，对于一个反对派人物来说，这已经非常多了。

sentences.en: So he has very much arrived on the national stage in Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实已经登上了俄罗斯的全国舞台。

sentences.en: Well, not quite yet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还不完全是。

sentences.en: Because in 2013, you know, he was still mostly known in Moscow and the big cities because his only platform really was the internet.
sentences.zh: 因为在2013年，他主要还是在莫斯科和大城市为人所知，因为他唯一的平台实际上就是互联网。

sentences.en: It was Twitter and it was his blog.
sentences.zh: 也就是推特和他的博客。

sentences.en: And what happens after 2013 is you see the internet access expand across Russia.
sentences.zh: 2013年之后发生的事情是，你看到互联网在俄罗斯的普及率扩大了。

sentences.en: And Navalny takes advantage of that using YouTube.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦利内利用了这一点，开始使用 YouTube。

sentences.en: And the most striking moment came in 2017 when Navalny puts out a video on what he describes as the hidden wealth of Dmitry Medvedev, the Russian prime minister at the time.
sentences.zh: 最引人注目的时刻出现在2017年，当时纳瓦利内发布了一段视频，描述了时任俄罗斯总理德米特里·梅德韦杰夫隐藏的财富。

sentences.en: You know, he goes into his yachts, his property in Italy, his hidden connections to Russian business tycoons.
sentences.zh: 他深入调查了梅德韦杰夫的游艇、在意大利的房产，以及他与俄罗斯商业大亨之间隐藏的联系。

sentences.en: You know, he claims that Medvedev essentially embezzled a billion dollars in change out of the Russian budget.
sentences.zh: 他声称梅德韦杰夫实际上从俄罗斯预算中贪污了十亿美元。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is the kind of stuff that many Russians suspect happens.
sentences.zh: 很多俄罗斯人其实都怀疑这种事情在发生。

sentences.en: But what's so different about Navalny's approach is that he puts it out there on YouTube in this really fast-paced, gripping style.
sentences.zh: 但纳瓦利内的方法与众不同之处在于，他以一种节奏极快、引人入胜的风格将其发布在 YouTube 上。

sentences.en: And it's a huge hit, this video gets millions of views within days.
sentences.zh: 这非常成功，视频在几天内就获得了数百万的点击量。

sentences.en: And then what Navalny does is he calls for protests across the country saying, we have to show the government that we will not accept this.
sentences.zh: 然后纳瓦利内号召全国范围内的抗议活动，说我们必须向政府表明我们不会接受这一点。

sentences.en: And kind of a guiding through line of Navalny's politics has been,
sentences.zh: 纳瓦利内政治理念的一条指导主线一直是，

sentences.en: elections are well and good, but that at the end of the day, this is an authoritarian system.
sentences.zh: 选举固然好，但归根结底，这是一个威权体制。

sentences.en: And the only real way to make our voice heard is to go out on the street.
sentences.zh: 而让我们的声音被听到的唯一真正途径就是走上街头。

sentences.en: And thousands of people come out all across the country in dozens of cities.
sentences.zh: 于是，全国几十个城市的成千上万民众走上了街头。

sentences.en: And so that really shows his potential to use the internet to mobilize people.
sentences.zh: 这确实展示了他利用互联网动员民众的潜力。

sentences.en: So what exactly is his goal?
sentences.zh: 那么他的目标到底是什么？

sentences.en: He's calling for protests.
sentences.zh: 他号召抗议。

sentences.en: He's clearly trying to weed out corruption from the government.
sentences.zh: 他显然是在试图清除政府中的腐败。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he has been seeking public office.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他一直在寻求担任公职。

sentences.en: So how are you making sense of all this?
sentences.zh: 你是如何理解这一切的？

sentences.en: Well, his goal, he's said it for years, is to take down Putin.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的目标，他多年来一直说，就是推翻普京。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: To change the political system in Russia.
sentences.zh: 改变俄罗斯的政治体制。

sentences.en: So he's explicit about it.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此表达得很明确。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: His marquee line starting in 2011 was,
sentences.zh: 他从2011年开始的标志性口号是，

sentences.en: Putin's party is a party of Zulikov-Ivarov, a party of crooks and thieves.
sentences.zh: 普京的政党是骗子和窃贼的政党。

sentences.en: Anton, I don't think of Vladimir Putin's Russia as a place that tolerates public criticism of its leadership.
sentences.zh: 安东，我不认为弗拉基米尔·普京的俄罗斯是一个容忍对其领导层公开批评的地方。

sentences.en: In fact, we know Putin has gone to extraordinary lengths to silence his enemies, dispatching operatives across the world to punish those who criticize him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们知道普京为了让敌人噤声采取了极端手段，派遣特工前往世界各地惩罚那些批评他的人。

sentences.en: So how is Navalny getting away with this?
sentences.zh: 那么纳瓦利内是怎么逃脱惩罚的呢？

sentences.en: It's a bit more complicated than that because for a long time, Putin's Kremlin has tried to create something they call managed democracy in Russia.
sentences.zh: 情况要复杂一些，因为长期以来，普京的克里姆林宫一直试图在俄罗斯创造一种他们所谓的“管理型民主”。

sentences.en: So there's a big middle class here.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个庞大的中产阶级。

sentences.en: There's a lot of exchange with the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 与西方有很多交流。

sentences.en: They really recognize that people here don't want this country to turn into North Korea or even China.
sentences.zh: 他们确实意识到这里的人民不希望这个国家变成朝鲜甚至中国。

sentences.en: People have become used to some degree of personal freedom of expression, to the Internet being free.
sentences.zh: 人们已经习惯了一定程度的个人表达自由，习惯了互联网的自由。

sentences.en: So basically, the Kremlin has for a long time tried to give people the feeling, some would say, the illusion of some degree of democracy.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，克里姆林宫长期以来一直试图给人们一种感觉，有些人会说是幻觉，即存在一定程度的民主。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，

sentences.en: many analysts make the argument that allowing opposition figures like Navalny to exist has allowed the Kremlin to give people in this country the feeling that they can make dissent heard without it ever actually threatening the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 许多分析人士认为，允许像纳瓦利内这样的反对派人物存在，使克里姆林宫能够让这个国家的人民觉得他们可以表达异见，而又不会真正威胁到克里姆林宫。

sentences.en: And also, there was clearly the decision made that Navalny was more of a danger to the Kremlin in jail than free.
sentences.zh: 而且，显然还有一个决定，那就是纳瓦利内在监狱里比在外面自由时对克里姆林宫的威胁更大。

sentences.en: Because going all the way in terms of putting him in prison would have run the risk of turning him into this totemic figure with the potential to unite the opposition.
sentences.zh: 因为彻底把他关进监狱会冒着让他变成一个具有团结反对派潜力的图腾式人物的风险。

sentences.en: So to summarize, Navalny is not seen as threat enough to actually punish or threaten directly.
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，纳瓦利内并没有被视为威胁到需要直接惩罚或威胁的程度。

sentences.en: And putting him in jail or worse might actually endanger this idea of managed democracy.
sentences.zh: 而且把他关进监狱或更糟，可能会危及这种“管理型民主”的理念。

sentences.en: So more or less, they're going to leave him alone.
sentences.zh: 所以差不多，他们打算让他自生自灭。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: Because also, let's remember, this was after Putin annexed Crimea and after the blow up of tensions with the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 因为还要记住，这是在普京吞并克里米亚以及与西方紧张关系爆发之后。

sentences.en: So that was all something that gave Putin this huge patriotic wave that he was riding on for several years.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都给了普京一股巨大的爱国浪潮，他在这股浪潮上乘风破浪了好几年。

sentences.en: You know, from 2014 into 2018, Putin's approval rating in independent polls was around 80%.
sentences.zh: 从2014年到2018年，普京在独立民调中的支持率约为80%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But that starts to change in 2018.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况在2018年开始改变。

sentences.en: First of all, that patriotic fervor around the annexation of Crimea has really gone away.
sentences.zh: 首先，围绕吞并克里米亚的那种爱国热情确实已经消退了。

sentences.en: And then that summer, the government does something that really sends these shockwaves throughout the Russian public,
sentences.zh: 然后那年夏天，政府做了一件在俄罗斯公众中引起巨大震动的事情，

sentences.en: which is they raise the pension age drastically by five years for men, by eight years for women.
sentences.zh: 那就是他们大幅提高了退休年龄，男性提高了五年，女性提高了八年。

sentences.en: So that summer of 2018 was really a watershed moment where Putin's really strong public approval started to dissipate quickly.
sentences.zh: 所以2018年的那个夏天确实是一个分水岭，普京非常强大的公众支持率开始迅速消散。

sentences.en: And then Navalny, at the same time, has been putting himself in position to take advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 而与此同时，纳瓦利内一直在为利用这一点做好准备。

sentences.en: So he tried to get on the ballot for the presidential election in 2018 when Putin was elected to his fourth term.
sentences.zh: 所以他在2018年普京竞选第四个任期时，试图参加总统选举。

sentences.en: The government, not very surprisingly, didn't let him get on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，政府没有让他参加竞选。

sentences.en: But what Navalny did nevertheless was build this physical infrastructure of campaign-style offices all across the country in dozens of Russian cities.
sentences.zh: 但纳瓦利内所做的是在全国几十个俄罗斯城市建立了竞选办公室的实体基础设施。

sentences.en: You know, really something that basically no other opposition figure has been able to do.
sentences.zh: 这确实是基本上没有其他反对派人物能够做到的事情。

sentences.en: So what that means is, just as Putin's popularity is fading, Navalny's ability to influence events across Russia has never been stronger.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，就在普京的支持率下滑时，纳瓦利内影响俄罗斯各地事件的能力却达到了前所未有的高度。

sentences.en: And we see more and more pressure from the government on Navalny's organization.
sentences.zh: 我们看到政府对纳瓦利内组织的压力越来越大。

sentences.en: We see very frequent raids against his offices, detention of supporters.
sentences.zh: 我们看到针对他办公室的频繁突袭，以及对支持者的拘留。

sentences.en: And it's really starting to feel like we're headed for a collision between Putin and Navalny.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们正走向普京和纳瓦利内之间的碰撞。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以越过付费墙，看看《纽约时报》的订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《纽约时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Anton, when does this collision come?
sentences.zh: 安东，这场碰撞什么时候发生？

sentences.en: So in August of last year, Navalny is in Siberia meeting with supporters ahead of local elections there.
sentences.zh: 去年8月，纳瓦利内在西伯利亚会见支持者，为那里的地方选举做准备。

sentences.en: Then he flies home to Moscow, and on that plane, soon after takeoff, he starts to feel sick.
sentences.zh: 然后他飞回莫斯科，在飞机起飞后不久，他开始感到不适。

sentences.en: He screams in pain.
sentences.zh: 他痛苦地尖叫。

sentences.en: He vomits.
sentences.zh: 他呕吐了。

sentences.en: He collapses.
sentences.zh: 他昏倒了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He falls into a coma.
sentences.zh: 他陷入了昏迷。

sentences.en: The pilot makes an emergency landing in the city of Omsk.
sentences.zh: 飞行员在鄂木斯克市进行了紧急降落。

sentences.en: And Navalny is met at the tarmac by an ambulance crew.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦利内在停机坪上被救护人员接走。

sentences.en: They determine he's been poisoned.
sentences.zh: 他们确定他中毒了。

sentences.en: They give him emergency treatment.
sentences.zh: 他们对他进行了紧急治疗。

sentences.en: He's taken to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 他被送往医院。

sentences.en: He's put on a ventilator.
sentences.zh: 他被戴上了呼吸机。

sentences.en: And then a standoff begins because his supporters are saying the guy's been poisoned.
sentences.zh: 随后僵局开始了，因为他的支持者说这家伙中毒了。

sentences.en: He needs help.
sentences.zh: 他需要帮助。

sentences.en: He needs to be airlifted somewhere out of the country for treatment.
sentences.zh: 他需要被空运到国外接受治疗。

sentences.en: But initially, the doctors don't let him leave.
sentences.zh: 但起初，医生不让他离开。

sentences.en: Angela Merkel, the German government, puts pressure on Russia to evacuate him to Berlin to let him go.
sentences.zh: 安格拉·默克尔和德国政府向俄罗斯施压，要求将其撤离到柏林，让他离开。

sentences.en: And eventually, he is let go.
sentences.zh: 最终，他被放行了。

sentences.en: He's flown directly to Berlin to the Charité Clinic, where doctors treat him.
sentences.zh: 他被直接飞往柏林的夏里特医院，医生在那里对他进行了治疗。

sentences.en: And within days, a special lab of the German military comes back with this really stunning finding that he was poisoned by a military-grade nerve agent called Novichok.
sentences.zh: 几天之内，德国军方的一个专门实验室得出了一个令人震惊的发现：他中了名为“诺维乔克”的军用级神经毒剂。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is the exact same military-grade poison that we know was used to attempt to assassinate different Putin enemies, including one in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 当然，这正是我们所知的曾被用于暗杀不同普京敌人的同一种军用级毒药，包括在英国发生的那起案件。

sentences.en: So the assumption has to be that Putin's government is behind this poisoning, right?
sentences.zh: 所以推测一定是普京政府在幕后策划了这次投毒，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, for the longest time, people assumed that this would not be something that the Russian government would want to do.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，长期以来，人们认为这不会是俄罗斯政府想要做的事情。

sentences.en: But when people heard it was Novichok, it was like, wow, this strongly points to the Russian state at the highest levels being involved.
sentences.zh: 但当人们听说那是“诺维乔克”时，就像是，哇，这强烈指向俄罗斯国家最高层参与其中。

sentences.en: So as this is playing out, Navalny actually almost miraculously starts to get better.
sentences.zh: 所以当这一切发生时，纳瓦利内竟然奇迹般地开始好转。

sentences.en: And he comes out of a coma later on in September.
sentences.zh: 他在9月晚些时候从昏迷中醒来。

sentences.en: And one of the first things he says is he's going to come back to Russia.
sentences.zh: 他说的第一件事就是他要回到俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That is a very unexpected instinct for someone who has been poisoned by Russia.
sentences.zh: 对于一个被俄罗斯投毒的人来说，这是一种非常出人意料的本能。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And also, we didn't even know at this point whether or not he'd be able to make a full recovery.
sentences.zh: 而且当时我们甚至不知道他是否能够完全康复。

sentences.en: He was in a coma for weeks.
sentences.zh: 他昏迷了几个星期。

sentences.en: And then he raises the stakes even further in December by marshalling evidence and publicly accusing Putin of having tried to kill him.
sentences.zh: 到了十二月，他通过收集证据并公开指控普京曾试图杀害他，将赌注进一步加大。

sentences.en: Well, what kind of evidence?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么样的证据呢？

sentences.en: Well, so he works with Bellingcat, this investigative journalism outlet that uses a lot of open source evidence.
sentences.zh: 他与“调查报道网站”（Bellingcat）合作，这是一个利用大量开源证据进行调查的新闻机构。

sentences.en: And they, together with a Russian outlet, The Insider, they basically get all these leaked telecommunications records out of Russia.
sentences.zh: 他们与俄罗斯的“内幕”网站（The Insider）联手，基本上从俄罗斯获取了所有泄露的电信记录。

sentences.en: And they piece those together along with flight records.
sentences.zh: 并将这些记录与航班记录拼凑在一起。

sentences.en: And they're able to show that a team of officers from Russia's domestic intelligence agency apparently followed Navalny around for years and were near him when he was presumably exposed to Novichok in Siberia right before he took that flight.
sentences.zh: 他们得以证明，俄罗斯国内情报机构的一支特工小组显然跟踪了纳瓦利内多年，并且在他于西伯利亚登机前疑似接触诺维乔克毒剂时，这些人就在他附近。

sentences.en: And then, sticking the knife in even further, Navalny releases a video a week later where he's actually calling.
sentences.zh: 随后，纳瓦利内更是雪上加霜，在一周后发布了一段视频，视频中他竟然打了一通电话。

sentences.en: He's on the phone with a member of this Russian team that was allegedly part of this assassination attempt.
sentences.zh: 他正在与俄罗斯团队的一名成员通话，此人据称参与了这次暗杀行动。

sentences.en: Navalny pretends to be a senior Russian official requesting a briefing from this officer and apparently successfully tricks him into essentially confessing the whole plot.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦利内假扮成一名俄罗斯高级官员，要求这名特工进行汇报，并显然成功地诱骗对方交代了整个阴谋。

sentences.en: That's extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, even down to the point that they apparently applied the poison to the inside seam of his underwear.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，甚至细致到他们显然是将毒药涂抹在他内裤的内缝上。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So Navalny is more or less fully recovered.
sentences.zh: 所以纳瓦利内基本上已经完全康复了。

sentences.en: He has made these videos embarrassing Putin's government.
sentences.zh: 他制作了这些让普京政府难堪的视频。

sentences.en: But is he really going to follow through and return to Moscow?
sentences.zh: 但他真的会坚持到底，回到莫斯科吗？

sentences.en: That's the question.
sentences.zh: 这才是问题所在。

sentences.en: Because also, the Russian government was increasingly making it absolutely clear that if Navalny comes back, he gets arrested.
sentences.zh: 因为俄罗斯政府也越来越明确地表示，如果纳瓦利内回来，他就会被捕。

sentences.en: And then, a couple weeks ago, one morning, Navalny posts on Instagram and says,
sentences.zh: 然后，几周前的一个早晨，纳瓦利内在Instagram上发帖说：

sentences.en: I'm coming back this Sunday.
sentences.zh: 我这周日回来。

sentences.en: I've bought a ticket.
sentences.zh: 我已经买好票了。

sentences.en: Come meet me at the airport.
sentences.zh: 来机场接我吧。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So a week ago, he boards a flight in Berlin to Moscow.
sentences.zh: 所以一周前，他登上了从柏林飞往莫斯科的航班。

sentences.en: Mr. Navalny from Israeli television, aren't you afraid?
sentences.zh: 纳瓦利内先生，来自以色列电视台，你不害怕吗？

sentences.en: Mr. Navalny from Israel.
sentences.zh: 来自以色列的纳瓦利内先生。

sentences.en: You know, this is such an extraordinary event.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真是一件非同寻常的事情。

sentences.en: And it's being live streamed in multiple places online.
sentences.zh: 而且它正在多个在线平台进行直播。

sentences.en: It's being watched by millions of people.
sentences.zh: 有数百万人正在观看。

sentences.en: Because everyone's like, so what's going to happen when he lands?
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都在想，他落地后会发生什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, will the Russians actually arrest him and risk setting off even more protests?
sentences.zh: 你知道，俄罗斯人真的会逮捕他，并冒着引发更多抗议的风险吗？

sentences.en: So hundreds of his supporters go out to Vnukovo airport, the airport where he's supposed to land.
sentences.zh: 于是，数百名支持者前往伏努科沃机场，也就是他预定降落的机场。

sentences.en: They're chanting.
sentences.zh: 他们在高呼口号。

sentences.en: The police try to keep them away.
sentences.zh: 警方试图将他们驱散。

sentences.en: They're starting to arrest some of his supporters who were there.
sentences.zh: 他们开始逮捕一些在场的支持者。

sentences.en: And minutes before it's supposed to land, you see the plane make a turn away from Moscow.
sentences.zh: 就在飞机预定降落前几分钟，你看到飞机掉头离开了莫斯科。

sentences.en: And then it turns out it's been diverted to a different airport.
sentences.zh: 结果发现它被改道飞往了另一个机场。

sentences.en: Allegedly, you know, according to the official version, because there was a stuck snow plow on the runway at the airport where he was supposed to land.
sentences.zh: 据官方说法称，是因为他原定降落的机场跑道上有一台除雪车卡住了。

sentences.en: Obviously, no one believes that.
sentences.zh: 显然，没人相信这一点。

sentences.en: But so everyone, all the journalists and supporters of his who were at Vnukovo airport rushed to try to get to Sheremetyevo airport.
sentences.zh: 但所有在伏努科沃机场的记者和支持者都匆忙赶往谢列梅捷沃机场。

sentences.en: So he ends up landing there and he's allowed off the plane.
sentences.zh: 他最终在那里降落，并被允许下机。

sentences.en: He gets onto the tarmac bus with all the other passengers.
sentences.zh: 他和其他乘客一起上了停机坪的摆渡车。

sentences.en: Before going into passport control, he very cinematically stops in front of a billboard that has a big picture of the Kremlin on it and gives the statement to journalists.
sentences.zh: 在进入护照检查处之前，他非常有电影感地停在一块印有克里姆林宫巨幅照片的广告牌前，向记者发表了声明。

sentences.en: You know, he's saying, I'm not afraid.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他说，我不害怕。

sentences.en: I'm so happy to be home.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能回家。

sentences.en: Then he heads to passport control where he's met by a group of police officers who tell him he is being detained.
sentences.zh: 然后他前往护照检查处，在那里被一群警察拦住，告知他已被拘留。

sentences.en: And what is he being detained for exactly?
sentences.zh: 他到底是因为什么被拘留的？

sentences.en: I mean, the government, it seems, has just poisoned him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，政府似乎刚刚对他下毒。

sentences.en: What has he allegedly done wrong?
sentences.zh: 他到底做错了什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They are saying he has violated the terms of his parole from a suspended prison sentence he received six years ago.
sentences.zh: 他们说他违反了六年前缓刑判决的假释条款。

sentences.en: By being in Germany and not properly notifying prison authorities about his whereabouts.
sentences.zh: 因为他身在德国，没有向监狱当局如实报告自己的行踪。

sentences.en: So he was taken to a police station near the airport.
sentences.zh: 于是他被带到了机场附近的一个警察局。

sentences.en: Then the next day, he's sentenced to 30 days in jail.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他被判入狱30天。

sentences.en: And before being taken to jail, he manages to record a video where he tells his supporters, you need to go out into the streets.
sentences.zh: 在被送往监狱之前，他设法录制了一段视频，告诉支持者：你们需要走上街头。

sentences.en: You need to proteSt.
sentences.zh: 你们需要抗议。

sentences.en: It's not just about me.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是为了我。

sentences.en: It's about your future.
sentences.zh: 这是为了你们的未来。

sentences.en: You know, his message is, this is the moment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他传达的信息是，就是现在。

sentences.en: They're trying to shut me down.
sentences.zh: 他们试图封杀我。

sentences.en: They're trying to shut our movement down.
sentences.zh: 他们试图封杀我们的运动。

sentences.en: And they're trying to show that this kind of authoritarian rule is possible in this country.
sentences.zh: 他们试图证明这种威权统治在这个国家是可能的。

sentences.en: And he's again telling his supporters the only way to really affect change in Russia is by protest in the streets.
sentences.zh: 他再次告诉支持者，在俄罗斯真正实现变革的唯一途径就是走上街头抗议。

sentences.en: Then his associates say these protests are going to happen on January 23rd.
sentences.zh: 随后他的同僚表示，这些抗议活动将于1月23日举行。

sentences.en: They start organizing these protests in dozens of cities across the country.
sentences.zh: 他们开始在全国数十个城市组织这些抗议活动。

sentences.en: But then the question becomes, okay, all these people are watching Navalny.
sentences.zh: 但问题随之而来，好吧，所有这些人都在关注纳瓦利内。

sentences.en: They know who he is.
sentences.zh: 他们知道他是谁。

sentences.en: They're even willing to support him maybe on social media.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可能愿意在社交媒体上支持他。

sentences.en: But are they willing to physically go out into the streets and risk their own well-being on his behalf?
sentences.zh: 但他们愿意为了他亲自走上街头，拿自己的安危去冒险吗？

sentences.en: And so the risk for Navalny out of all that is, what if all these people don't show up?
sentences.zh: 所以纳瓦利内面临的风险是，如果这些人都不出现怎么办？

sentences.en: And this really becomes a key test for his movement.
sentences.zh: 这确实成为了对他运动的一次关键考验。

sentences.en: So what ends up happening on Saturday?
sentences.zh: 那么周六到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: So Navalny's supporters had said, go out into the streets at 2 p.m.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦利内的支持者曾呼吁，在当地时间下午2点走上街头。

sentences.en: local time.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯有11个时区。

sentences.en: Russia has 11 time zones.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着当抗议者开始出现在俄罗斯太平洋沿岸时，莫斯科这里还是深夜。

sentences.en: So that meant it was still the middle of the night here in Moscow when protesters started emerging on Russia's Pacific coaSt.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，那股抗议浪潮席卷了全国。

sentences.en: As the day progressed, you know, that wave of protest kind of rolled across the country.
sentences.zh: 它到达了世界上最冷的城市雅库茨克，那里的气温是零下60华氏度。

sentences.en: It hit the city of Yakutsk, the coldest city in the world where it was negative 60 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 我们一次又一次地看到数百甚至数千人在街头抗议。

sentences.en: And over and over again, we saw hundreds, sometimes thousands of people protesting in the streets.
sentences.zh: 你知道，周六下午我身处莫斯科市中心的普希金广场。

sentences.en: You know, I was in Pushkin Square here in central Moscow on a Saturday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 广场上挤满了人，高呼着“普京是窃贼”。

sentences.en: And people were totally packing that square, chanting, Putin is a thief.
sentences.zh: 警方在很大程度上允许人们聚集。

sentences.en: The police, for the most part, let people gather.
sentences.zh: 但他们随后仍使用相当暴力的手段驱散人群。

sentences.en: But then they still used rather violent methods to get the crowd to disperse.
sentences.zh: 我们反复看到防暴警察，穿着迷彩服，戴着闪亮的黑色头盔，身穿防弹衣，冲向抗议者，挥舞警棍，试图清空广场。

sentences.en: We repeatedly saw riot police, you know, in camouflage, in shiny black helmets, in body armor, charging at the protesters, swinging their batons, trying to clear the square.
sentences.zh: 圣彼得堡发生了一件可怕的事，相关视频在俄罗斯社交媒体上疯传。

sentences.en: There was this awful video out of St. Petersburg, which has been really ricocheting through social media in Russia,
sentences.zh: 一名女子走向一名正在拘留他人的防暴警察。

sentences.en: where a woman walks up to a riot police officer who's detaining someone else.
sentences.zh: 那名警察径直走到她面前，狠狠地踢了她的肚子，力道之大导致她被送进了医院。

sentences.en: And that police officer just goes up to her and kicks her incredibly hard in the stomach, so hard she's gone to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这里看到了非常激烈的场面。

sentences.en: So we have these really intense scenes here.
sentences.zh: 但令人惊讶的是，人们往往坚守阵地，甚至反抗防暴警察。

sentences.en: But people surprisingly stood their ground often, even fighting back against the riot police,
sentences.zh: 这是这些抗议活动与我们过去所见有很大不同的一点。

sentences.en: which is one way in which these protests were really different from a lot of what we saw in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 有一个时刻非常引人注目，一辆政府黑色轿车经过，车顶闪着那种蓝色的官方警灯。

sentences.en: There was one moment really striking where a black government car drove by with one of those blue official lights on top.
sentences.zh: 人们先是开始向它投掷雪球。

sentences.en: And people first started throwing snowballs at it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们冲上去，开始跳上车顶并踢踹车身，甚至导致司机受伤。

sentences.en: Then they rushed at it and started jumping on it and kicking it, actually injuring the driver.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是抗议者表现出的一种我们以前几乎从未见过的胆量。

sentences.en: You know, this was a degree of brazenness on the part of protesters we really pretty much haven't seen before.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，俄罗斯人通过现身并表达对普京政府的厌恶，回应了纳瓦利内的号召。

sentences.en: So very clearly, Russians answered Navalny's call by showing up and expressing their disgust with the Putin government.
sentences.zh: 他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 他们回应了他的号召。

sentences.en: They answered his call.
sentences.zh: 这些人数还不足以迫使克里姆林宫在几天内改变方针。

sentences.en: These weren't numbers that we can expect to force the Kremlin to change course within days.
sentences.zh: 但他们明确表明，纳瓦利内已经成为反对派的象征。

sentences.en: But they made it clear that Navalny has become a symbol of the opposition.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们昨天在全国各地采访了许多参加集会的人，他们说，我甚至并不真正支持纳瓦利内。

sentences.en: You know, there were lots of people we spoke to who attended rallies all over the country yesterday who said, I don't even really support Navalny.
sentences.zh: 我不赞同他所有的观点。

sentences.en: I don't agree with all his ideas.
sentences.zh: 但现在，我们正目睹当权者如此不公、如此不义，我们必须做出回应。

sentences.en: But right now, this is a moment where we're seeing such unfairness, such injustice on the part of those in power that we need to respond.
sentences.zh: 所以这已经成为一个时刻，真正凝聚了人们对经济状况、司法状况和腐败问题积压已久的挫败感。

sentences.en: So this has become kind of this moment that really crystallizes all this pent-up frustration that people have with the economic situation,
sentences.zh: 人们真正围绕着身陷囹圄的纳瓦利内这一象征团结了起来。

sentences.en: with the judicial situation, with corruption.
sentences.zh: 就这里正在进行的运动广度而言，至关重要的一点是，这些抗议活动不仅仅发生在莫斯科和圣彼得堡。

sentences.en: People have really come together around the symbol of Navalny in jail.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅仅发生在全国各大城市。

sentences.en: And in terms of the breadth of the movement that's going on here, what's absolutely key, too, is that these protests didn't just happen in Moscow and St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 据统计，周六俄罗斯有109个城市举行了抗议活动。

sentences.en: They didn't just happen in major cities across the country.
sentences.zh: 想想看，109个城市同时举行了支持阿列克谢·纳瓦利内的抗议活动。

sentences.en: According to one count, they took place in 109 cities across Russia on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 那么，说这种策略对普京适得其反，他将阿列克谢·纳瓦利内变成了一股更强大的力量，并对普京政府构成了更大的威胁，这公平吗？

sentences.en: Think about that, 109 cities saw coordinated protests in favor of Alexei Navalny.
sentences.zh: 是的，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: So is it fair to say that this strategy has backfired for Putin, that he has turned Alexei Navalny into an even more powerful force and an even bigger threat to Putin's government?
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，政府在过去六个月里，尤其是过去几周里对纳瓦利内采取的强硬路线，确实使他成为了一个具有巨大全国影响力的人物。

sentences.en: Yes, no question.
sentences.zh: 那么现在会发生什么？

sentences.en: I think that's become very clear that the hard line that the government has pursued against Navalny over the last six months
sentences.zh: 他还在监狱里。

sentences.en: and certainly over the last couple of weeks has really turned him into a figure of really large national stature.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what happens now?
sentences.zh: 他还在监狱里。

sentences.en: He's still in jail.
